• Strun: Deals 50 Shock damage to Health and Magicka.

• Gaar: Deals 75 Shock damage to Health and Magicka.

• Kest: Deals 100 Shock damage to Health and Magicka.

Marked for Death

Cooldown: 60/90/120.

• Krii: Reduces enemy Health by 50 and Armor Rating by 50 for 30 seconds.

• Lun: Reduces enemy Health by 75 and Armor Rating by 100 for 30 seconds.

• Aus: Reduces enemy Health by 100 and Armor Rating by 150 for 30 seconds.

Poison Breath

Cooldown: 60/90/120 seconds

• Laas: Deals 7.5 Poison damage per second for 10 seconds.

• Slen: Deals 11.25 Poison damage per second for 10 seconds.

• Aus: Deals 15 Poison damage per second for 10 seconds.

Slow Time

Cooldown: 180/240/300 seconds.

• Tiid: Slows time by 50% for 10 seconds.

• Klo: Slows time by 50% for 20 seconds.

• Ul: Slows time by 50% for 30 seconds.

Soul Tear

Cooldown: 120/150/180 seconds.

• Rii: Deals 5 Magic damage per second for 10 seconds.

• Vaaz: Deals 7.5 Magic damage per second for 10 seconds. If the target dies, fills a soul gem.

• Zol: Deals 10 Magic damage per second for 10 seconds. If the target dies, fills a soul gem and reanimates their corpse.

Storm Call

Cooldown: 180/240/300 seconds.

• Strun: Calls a storm for 30 seconds. Lightning bolts from the storm deal 50 damage.

• Bah: Calls a storm for 45 seconds. Lightning bolts from the storm deal 75 damage.

• Qo: Calls a storm for 60 seconds. Lightning bolts from the storm deal 100 damage.

Subdue

Cooldown: 60/90/120 seconds.

• Zun: Reduces enemy weapon damage by 25% for 20 seconds.

• Haal: Reduces enemy weapon damage by 25% for 40 seconds.

• Viik: Reduces enemy weapon damage by 25% for 60 seconds.

Summon Durnehviir

Cooldown: 5/10/300 seconds.

• Dur: No effect.

• Neh: No effect.

• Viir: Summons Durnehviir.

Throw Voice

Cooldown: 30/20/10 seconds.

• Zul: Throws voice.

• Mey: Throws voice.

• Gut: Throws voice.

Unrelenting Force

Cooldown: 10/20/30 seconds.

• Fus: Deals a 75% stagger to enemies.

• Ro: Deals a 100% stagger to enemies.

• Dah: Deals a 100% stagger and ragdolls enemies.

Whirlwind Sprint

Cooldown: 10/20/30 seconds.

• Wuld: Rush forward by 30 feet.

• Nah: Rush forward by 40 feet.

• Kest: Rush forward by 50 feet.

Meditations

Stormcrown overhauls Paarthurnax's Meditation mechanic to provide upgrades for almost all Shouts. When you approach Paarthurnax for the first time, you will be able to ask him whether he teaches the power of the Voice to others. Doing so will lead to Paarthurnax offering to teach you to meditate on the Words of Power. Step towards the Word Wall on which Paarthurnax is perched to begin.

Meditating on a Word of Power consumes a dragon soul, and provides a permanent upgrade to the chosen Shout. You can only meditate on the Words of Power for Shouts which you have mastered by learning and unlocking all three words. Unlike Vanilla, you can have more than one Meditation effect at a time.

Animal Ally: Your Animal Ally's Armor Rating is increased by 150, and their Magic Resistance is increased by 25%.

Battle Fury: Battle Fury increases the Armor Rating of all nearby allies by up to 150.

Become Ethereal: Become Ethereal restores Health over time.

Cyclone: Cyclone deals extra damage over 10 seconds.

Dismay: Dismay works on the undead, Daedra, and Dwarven automatons.

Dragon Aspect: Dragon Aspect does not trigger a Shout cooldown.

Dragonrend: Dragonrend reduces Armor Rating by 150 and Magic Resistance by 25%.

Drain Vitality: Drain Vitality absorbs twice as much Health, Magicka, and Stamina.

Elemental Fury: Elemental Fury reduces the cost of power attacking and drawing a bow by 25%.

Fire Breath: Fire Breath ignites enemies and leaves a trail of fire on the ground.

Frost Breath: Frost Breath deals extra Stamina damage over 30 seconds.

Ice Form: Ice From has a chance to encase enemies in ice for 10 seconds.

Kyne's Peace: Kyne’s Peace works on the undead, Daedra, and Dwarven automatons.

Lightning Breath: Lightning Breath deals extra Magicka damage over 30 seconds.

Marked for Death: Marked for Death reduces enemy Magic Resistance by up to 25%.

Poison Breath: Poison Breath deals double damage to enemies who fall below half Health.

Slow Time: Slow Time is twice as strong.

Soul Tear: Soul Tear deals extra damage over 10 seconds.

Subdue: Subdue reduces enemy weapon damage by an additional 25%.

Unrelenting Force: Unrelenting Force deals additional damage and breaks through wards.

Epistolary Acumen

The Black Book Epistolary Acumen now grants you one of three possible buffs to Dragon Aspect. These buffs are:

Dragonborn Force: Dragon Aspect reduces incoming damage while power attacking, drawing a bow, or casting a spell by 25% .

Dragonborn Might: Dragon Aspect increases your Armor Rating by an additional 100.

Dragonborn Soul: Dragon Aspect increases your Fire, Frost, and Shock Resistance by 25%.

Notes

• The words for the new Lightning Breath Shout can be fold in Yngvild's Gulf, to the east of Dushnikh Yal, and in an ashy area on southern Solstheim, respectively.

• The words for the new Poison Breath Shout can be found in Bleakcoast Cave, in the Morthal Swamp, and in the Snowclad Ruins in Solstheim, respectively.

• Elemental Fury's Meditation requires you to have the unarmed weapon equipped to work. The unarmed weapon is an invisible weapon that the game equips on the player in certain circumstances. All major perk overhauls (Ordinator, Adamant, Vokrii, etc) apply the unarmed weapon to the character as part of their unarmed support, so we have not reduplicated that feature here.

• Slow Time is not affected by perks that extend its duration, because of the way it interacts with them. This does not apply to its Meditation effect.

• The Subdue Shout is a reinterpretation of the Disarm Shout, and works both for the player and for enemies.

Compatibility

Stormcrown requires Address Library for SKSE Plugins and the most recent version of Custom Skills Framework, which is only compatible with Skyrim Special Edition and Anniversary Edition 1.6.640 (Steam) and 1.6.659 (GOG). Stormcrown's edits are kept to a minimum, meaning it should not cause any major compatibility issues with your game. Stormcrown should not be combined with other Shout overhauls, such as Thunderchild or Forceful Tongue.

items.description:
External links

https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/110/images/68425-0-1489347895.pngSupport Enai Siaion on Patreon!

Discuss this mod on /r/EnaiRim or the Enairim Discord

Features

• Sacrilege is a clean and balanced vampire and Vampire Lord overhaul.[/*]

• Blood magic and racial bonuses.[/*]

• Reverse progression: vampires are stronger, not weaker, when recently fed.[/*]

• Long term progression in the form of vampire ranks, blood magic and Vampiric Drain upgrades.[/*]

• Vampire lords get a stronger identity and incentives to switch between melee and caster stance.[/*]

• Lightweight scripts, no save bloat.[/*]

• Can be installed during your playthrough (as long as you are not currently a vampire).[/*]

Life as a vampire

Vampire abilities

Vampirism is a gift in some ways, a curse in others. You gain the following generic Vampire abilities:

• Champion of the Night: Your Vampiric charm improves your Illusion spells to work on targets up to 15-40* levels higher.[/*]

• Fierce Hunger: Able to Feed on sleeping or seduced people to sate your Vampiric hunger, or lethally Drain them.[/*]

• Haunted Lakes: Your Vampiric blood allows you to breathe underwater. While submersed, you are protected from Sunlight.[/*]

• Nightstalker's Footsteps: Your Vampiric blood makes you 15-40*% harder to detect by creatures and people while sneaking.[/*]

• Resist Disease: Your Vampiric blood gives you immunity to disease.[/*]

• Resist Frost: Your Vampiric blood gives you 50/40/30/20% resistance to Frost.[/*]

• Resist Poison: Your Vampiric blood gives you 100% resistance to Poison.[/*]

• Unnatural Strength: Your Vampiric blood increases movement speed by 10% and attack damage by 5-30*%.

• Forsaken: Your Vampiric curse weakens Divine blessings by 75-25*%.[/*]

• Mockery of Life: Your Vampiric blood makes you 50-25*% less susceptible to healing spells and effects.[/*]

• Weakness to Fire: Your Vampiric blood gives you 20/30/40/50% weakness to Fire.[/*]

• Weakness to Sunlight: Health, Magicka, and Stamina do not recover while in Sunlight and are reduced by 25/50/75/100 points.[/*]

As your Vampiric hunger increases, your Resist Frost grows weaker and Weakness to Fire and Weakness to Sunlight grow stronger. For the meaning of the asterisk next to a value, see "Vampire ranks".

Additionally, you gain a racial Vampire ability:

• (Argonian) Aquatic Predator: Your Argonian blood allows you to sate your Vampiric hunger by catching docile fish.[/*]

• (Breton) Dolmen Haunt: Your Breton heritage allows you to sate your Vampiric hunger by activating a Standing Stone, once a day.[/*]

• (Dark Elf) Promiscuous: Your Dark Elven blood copies the racial Vampire ability of the race you prey on. You can have only one at a time.[/*]

• (High Elf) Pale Gold: Your High Elven blood slows Vampiric hunger by 50% and you gain Vampiric ranks 15% faster, if you are Sated.[/*]

• (Imperial) Connoisseur: Your Imperial sophistication enables you to bottle a Potion of Blood or Thaumaturgy when you Drain a victim.[/*]

• (Khajiit) Prey Drive: Your Khajiit fangs enable you to sate your Vampiric hunger by using or consuming Human Flesh or Human Hearts.[/*]

• (Nord) Preserved Blood: Your Nord heritage grants 10% to bottle a Potion of Blood or Thaumaturgy when looting people you killed.[/*]

• (Orc) Battle Hunger: Your Orc strength enables you to Feed or Drain in combat by activating an enemy person who is bleeding out.[/*]

• (Redguard) Mummified Body: Your Redguard blood slows Vampiric hunger by 50% and you gain Vampiric ranks 15% faster.[/*]

• (Wood Elf) Blood Hunt: Your Wood Elven heritage grants 10% to bottle a Potion of Blood or Thaumaturgy when looting animals you killed.[/*]

Khajiit also have a hidden racial bonus that grants 5% chance to loot a Human Flesh or Human Heart from people you killed.

Vampire spells

In vanilla Skyrim, your only option for Vampiric blood magic is the underwhelming Vampiric Drain. Sacrilege not only allows it to scale in various ways, but adds three other Hemomancy spells that are unlocked through Vampire Lord perks.

• (Novice) Vampiric Drain: Absorb 5-30* points of Health per second from a living target.[/*]

• (Perk unlock - Apprentice) Vampiric Seed: Bone shards pierce a living target, absorbing 1-6* Health and dealing 1-6* magic damage for 5 seconds.[/*]

• (Perk unlock - Adept) Vampiric Orb: Impales living targets in the area, absorbing 2-12* Health and dealing 2-12* magic damage for 5 seconds.[/*]

• (Perk unlock - Expert) Vampiric Cloak: Bats attack living targets for 60 seconds. Absorbs 1-6* Health and deals 1-6* magic damage per second.[/*]

Vampiric Drain scales strongly into the late game. In addition to scaling with Vampire rank, it is improved by the Hemomancer perk, adding up to 42 absorb per second at 100 Destruction skill. Drain also stuns if dual cast. For the meaning of the asterisk next to a value, see "Vampire ranks".

Vampire powers

Your Vampiric powers in vanilla Skyrim are 1/day greater powers that merely replicate effects you can already cast at will. Sacrilege improves them by making their effects more unique and changing them to at-will powers, at the cost of increasing your Vampiric hunger by one stage each time they are used.

• (Lost: Hungry) Vampire's Shroud: Expend some of your blood to protect yourself against Sunlight for 30-180* seconds. Increases Vampiric hunger.[/*]

• (Lost: Famished) Vampire's Scream: Living targets within range flee for 10-60* seconds and can be seen through walls. Increases Vampiric hunger.[/*]

• (Lost: Blood Starved) Vampire's Shadow: Turn into mist, becoming invisible and sneaking 25% better for 30-180* seconds. Increases Vampiric hunger.[/*]

• Vampire's Seduction: Bewitches a person up to level 10 for 10-60* seconds, calming them and allowing you to feed.[/*]

• Vampire's Sight: Improved night vision. Cast again to disable.[/*]

Vampire's Seduction trivialises feeding in vanilla Skyrim. It is much less effective in Sacrilege, with a low level cap that matches the level of most townsfolk, making it primarily a tool for sating your Vampiric hunger in cities, with racial Vampire abilities and other methods of feeding taking its place in the field. For the meaning of the asterisk next to a value, see "Vampire ranks".

Vampiric hunger

Progression:

As in vanilla Skyrim, you start as a Sated vampire, and Vampiric hunger increases by one stage per in-game day. The Vampire ability tracks your current hunger stage.

• Sated[/*]

• Hungry[/*]

• Famished[/*]

• Blood Starved[/*]

The following effects modify the progression of Vampiric hunger:

• Vampire rank: Slows the progression of Vampiric hunger by 0-100*%.[/*]

• Pale Gold (High Elf): Slows the progression of Vampiric hunger by 100% when you are Sated.[/*]

• Mummified Body (Redguard): Slows the progression of Vampiric hunger by 50%.[/*]

To compensate for the Vampire's Seduction nerf making it harder to stay fed than in vanilla Skyrim, hunger progression is slowed down as your Vampire rank increases. For the meaning of the asterisk next to a value, see "Vampire ranks".

Effects:

As Vampiric hunger increases, your Resist Frost grows weaker and Weakness to Fire and Weakness to Sunlight grow stronger. Moreover, powers are gradually lost. See "Vampire abilities" and "Vampire powers".

When you become Blood Starved, neutral citizens will attack you on sight (a classic Skyrim feature removed by Dawnguard). Additionally, you will take 1 sun damage per second in Sunlight. Taking sun damage also prevents waiting and fast travelling, so the only ways to prevent the damage are hiding indoors or underwater or an active Vampire's Shroud power.

Feeding:

To sate your Vampiric hunger, activate a sleeping person or a person affected by the Vampire's Seduction power and choose the Feed or Drain option. Both options restore your hunger status to Sated and heal you (40 + 4*target level) points (up to level 50). The Drain option additionally kills the target, grants Destruction experience and advances your Vampire rank progression by 24 hours.

The vanilla feed animation is brittle and breaks easily, especially when feeding on awake targets that are not on the same elevation as you. This is not a bug with Sacrilege.

Vampire ranks

Vampires become more powerful as they grow older, attaining higher Vampire ranks. The Vampire ability tracks your progression towards the next rank in in-game hours. You progress towards your next Vampire rank as follows:

As a mortal:

• Time: Each in-game hour increases Vampire rank progression by 1 hour.[/*]

• Drain people: Each victim increases Vampire rank progression by 24 hours.[/*]

• Consume Potions of Thaumaturgy: Each potion increases Vampire rank progression by 24 hours.[/*]

The following effects modify the progression of Vampire ranks:

• Aquatic Predator (Argonian): Feeding on docile fish increases Vampire rank progression by 2 hours.[/*]

• Dolmen Haunt (Breton): Feeding on a standing stone increases Vampire rank progression by 6 hours.[/*]

• Pale Gold (High Elf): Each in-game hour increases Vampire rank progression by an additional 0.3 hours if Sated.[/*]

• Prey Drive (Khajiit): Using or consuming Human Flesh or Human Hearts increases Vampire rank progression by 6 hours.[/*]

• Mummified Body (Redguard): Each in-game hour increases Vampire rank progression by an additional 0.15 hours.[/*]

As a Vampire Lord:

• Time: Each in-game hour increases Vampire rank progression by an additional 1 hour.[/*]

• Perform power attack bites: Each victim increases Vampire rank progression by 24 hours.[/*]

• Gain Blood Points: Each Blood Point increases Vampire rank progression by 2 hours.[/*]

The available ranks are as follows:

• Fledgeling: Starting rank[/*]

• Blooded: 10 days[/*]

• Mistwalker: 15 days (total 25 days)[/*]

• Nightstalker: 25 days (total 50 days)[/*]

• Nightlord: 45 days (total 95 days)[/*]

• Nightmaster: 85 days (total 180 days)[/*]

Raising your Vampire rank improves many Vampire abilities, spells and powers. This is indicated on the mod page by an asterisk next to a number range. It also slows the progression of Vampiric hunger.

Fast travelling and waiting only count as 1 hour, no matter how long the process takes. This prevents certain AFK exploits to rapidly gain Vampire ranks. The higher Vampire ranks are a long term form of progression and are not intended to be able to be rushed. Note that since version 2.0.0, every race has a racial ability that contributes towards Vampire ranks in some form, either directly or by granting Potions of Thaumaturgy or allowing you to Drain more often.

Alchemy

The following potion recipes are now available:

• (1x Flawless Ruby + 1x Vampire Dust) Potion of Embracing: Grants Vampirism unless you are immune to diseases. Vampires heal 100 points of Health.[/*]

• (1x Void Salts + 1x Vampire Dust) Potion of Hunger: Increases Vampiric hunger. Vampires heal 100 points of Health.[/*]

The Court's Chef perk enables you to create the following potions:

• (2x Human Flesh or 2x Human Heart) Potion of Blood: Alleviates Vampiric hunger. Vampires heal 100 points of Health.[/*]

• (1x Human Flesh or 1x Human Heart) Potion of Viscera: Advances Vampire Lord perk progression. Vampires heal 100 points of Health.[/*]

• (3x Human Flesh or 3x Human Heart) Potion of Thaumaturgy: Increases Vampiric rank progression by 24 hours. Vampires heal 100 points of Health.[/*]

• (10x Human Flesh or 10x Human Heart + 2x Moon Sugar + 2x Fire Salts + 1x Vampire Dust) Potion of Purging: Cures Vampirism. Vampires heal 100 points of Health.[/*]

Life as a Vampire Lord

In vanilla Skyrim, vampire lord spells are universally useful, denying vampire lords a unique identity with strengths and weaknesses. Sacrilege makes them especially powerful at area effect damage, balanced by high Magicka costs and the need to switch into melee stance to replenish Magicka, making them weaker against single targets.

Basic stats

You gain the following effects in vampire lord form:

• Able to loot corpses and containers[/*]

• Carry weight increased by 500 points[/*]

• Take no damage from falls[/*]

• Vampire lord attacks deal 10 (+1 per character level) base damage (up to level 50)[/*]

• Undead skin grants 50 (+5 per character level) base armor (up to level 50)[/*]

• Undead skin grants 10% (+1% per character level) magic resistance (up to level 50)[/*]

• Waterwalking[/*]

• Able to feed by performing a melee kill move (power attack bite)[/*]

• Power attacks always stagger targets[/*]

• Regenerate 10% of maximum Magicka per second (only in melee stance)[/*]

• Regenerate 5% of maximum Stamina per second (only in caster stance)[/*]

• Bloodthirst: Vampire lord claws do 5-30* points of bleed damage, healing you for the same amount.[/*]

• Feast: Killing a person with a melee kill move (power attack bite) restores 200 points of Health.[/*]

Note that Magicka only regenerates in melee stance and Stamina only regenerates in caster stance, creating an incentive to "stance dance".

Scaling and experience gain

A major drawback of vampire lords in vanilla Skyrim is their lack of skill scaling and inability to gain experience. In Sacrilege, vampire lords scale with your Destruction skill:

• In vampire lord form, gain +0.25 damage per level of Destruction, and +1.5 armor per level of Destruction (up to level 100).[/*]

• In vampire lord form, use the Raze, Vampiric Grip or Gutwrench spell in caster stance, attack in melee stance or perform a melee kill move (power attack bite) to gain experience in Destruction.[/*]

• In vampire lord form, use the Conjure Gargoyle spell in caster stance to gain experience in Conjuration.[/*]

• In vampire lord form, use the Vampiric Grip or Maelstrom spell in caster stance to gain experience in Alteration.[/*]

• In mortal form, Drain a victim to gain experience in Destruction.[/*]

• In both forms, damaging Vampiric blood spells are considered Destruction spells for the purpose of Destruction perks.[/*]

Vampire Lord spells (Blood Magic)

Similar to vanilla Skyrim, but with a stronger focus on damage instead of disabling effects.

• Raze: Cuts through living targets in a line, absorbing 10-60* Health and dealing 10-60* magic damage. (Magicka: 50)[/*]

• Conjure Gargoyle: Vampiric power summons a Gargoyle for 60-360* seconds. (Magicka: 100)[/*]

• (Perk unlock) Gutwrench: Absorb 5-30* Health per second from nearby living targets. After 1 second per 25 Health, they explode. (Magicka: 25/sec)[/*]

• (Perk unlock) Vampiric Grip: Pulls a living target to you, absorbing 10-60* Health and Stamina per second at close range. (Magicka: 50/sec)[/*]

• (Perk unlock) Maelstrom: Vortex pulls targets within range to the center, inflicting 50% weakness to magic for 3 seconds. (Magicka: 200)[/*]

Gutwrench affects a 20 foot area around yourself as you concentrate. The secondary effect causes it to build up 25 points of tension per second as you keep it on enemies for a prolonged period of time, ultimately tearing them apart when this tension exceeds their remaining Health. Built up tension is reset when they leave the radius.

Maximum Raze damage is 168 (120 * 1.4 from Hemomancer).

Vampire Lord powers (Night Powers)

Similar to vanilla Skyrim, but with a stronger focus on crowd control.

• Bats: Transform into a swarm of bats and dash a short distance. (2 uses, 20 second cooldown, Magicka: 25)[/*]

• Echo Scream: Sends out a quick pulse that detects all creatures. (Magicka: 15)[/*]

• (Perk unlock) Mist Form: Turn into invisible and invulnerable mist for 10 seconds, regenerating 10 Health, Magicka and Stamina per second. (1 use, 60 second cooldown, Magicka: 100)[/*]

• (Perk unlock) Supernatural Reflexes: Slow time for 10 seconds as you move and attack faster and your power attacks knock targets down. (1 use, 40 second cooldown, Magicka: 200)[/*]

• (Perk unlock) Tremor: Shake the earth, staggering nearby targets and throwing them into the air. (2 uses, 30 second cooldown, Magicka: 100)[/*]

Vampire Lord perks

Sacrilege expands the Vampire Lord perk tree from 11 to 24 perks.

As in vanilla Skyrim, absorb lifeblood to progress towards the next Vampire Lord perk point. It takes 2 lifeblood absorptions to gain your first perk point, increased by 1 for each further perk point (down from 2 in vanilla Skyrim to compensate for the increased number of perks). In version 2.2.0 and later, you also gain lifeblood by using Vampiric Drain and Hemomancy spells in humanoid form once you have unlocked Vampire Lord.

• Killing victims with Raze or Gutwrench: Each victim grants lifeblood.[/*]

• Performing power attack bites: Each victim grants lifeblood.[/*]

• Consume Potions of Viscera: Each potion grants lifeblood.[/*]

Spend the points on the following Vampire Lord perks:

• Scion: As a Vampire Lord, gain a 50 point bonus to all attributes (Health, Magicka, Stamina).[/*]

• Unearthly Will: As a Vampire Lord, all spells and powers cost 25% less to cast.[/*]

• Night Cloak: As a Vampire Lord, a cloud of bats absorbs 5 Health per second from each nearby living enemy in combat.[/*]

• Energy Vampire: As a Vampire Lord, your attacks also absorb Magicka and your damaging spells also absorb Stamina.[/*]

• Shapechanger: As a Vampire Lord, your attacks weaken targets to your damaging spells and your damaging spells weaken targets to your attacks, increasing damage by 25% for 10 seconds.[/*]

• Fountain of Blood: Draining a person or killing a person with a power attack bite restores three times as much Health and also restores Magicka and Stamina.[/*]

• Slasher: As a Vampire Lord, your power attacks are 25% stronger and hit all targets in front of you.[/*]

• Hemomancer: Vampiric blood spells deal 0.4% more damage per level of Destruction.[/*]

• Blood Storm: As a Vampire Lord, upgrades your Raze spell to Blood Storm, which deals 15% more damage and can be held down for rapid fire.[/*]

• Auspex: Your Vampiric senses warn you when enemies approach within 150 feet, briefly revealing them.[/*]

• Court's Chef: Able to create a variety of beneficial Potions from Human Flesh or Human Hearts at a cooking pot.[/*]

• Wings of the Strix: As a Vampire Lord, sprinting in caster stance allows you to glide, greatly reducing fall speed.[/*]

• Gutwrench: Blood Magic: Absorb Health from nearby living targets, tearing them apart when maintained for long enough.[/*]

• Vampiric Grip: Blood Magic: Pulls a living target to you from a distance, absorbing Health and Stamina at close range.[/*]

• Maelstrom: Blood Magic: Vortex pulls targets within range to the center, briefly weakening them to magic.[/*]

• Mist Form: Night Power: Turn into invisible and invulnerable mist, regenerating Health, Magicka and Stamina.[/*]

• Supernatural Reflexes: Night Power: Slow time as you move and attack faster and your power attacks knock targets down.[/*]

• Tremor: Night Power: Shake the earth, staggering nearby targets and throwing them into the air.[/*]

• Vampiric Seed: Mortal Hemomancy: Bone shards pierce a living target, absorbing Health and dealing magic damage.[/*]

• Vampiric Orb: Mortal Hemomancy: Impales living targets in the area, absorbing Health and dealing magic damage.[/*]

• Vampiric Cloak: Mortal Hemomancy: Bats attack living targets. Absorbs Health and deals magic damage.[/*]

• Blood From a Stone: Vampiric blood spells can now damage nonliving targets.[/*]

• Starving Artist: Vampiric blood spells absorb Stamina equal to 50% of damage dealt.[/*]

• Make Them Beautiful: Vampiric blood spells tear apart targets below 25% Health, killing them instantly.[/*]

Recommended mods

Sacrilege is part of a cycle of vanilla-plus gameplay overhauls that combine to form "V++ Enairim", designed to improve existing game systems without drastically changing the game:

• Odin - Skyrim Magic Overhaul[/*]

• Vokrii - Minimalistic Perks of Skyrim[/*]

• Mannaz - Integrated Races of Skyrim[/*]

• Freyr - Integrated Standing Stones of Skyrim[/*]

• Valravn - Integrated Combat of Skyrim[/*]

• Growl - Werebeasts of Skyrim[/*]

• Sacrilege - Minimalistic Vampires of Skyrim[/*]

• Trua - Minimalistic Faiths of Skyrim[/*]

My "V++" overhauls can be used interchangeably with my "full size" overhauls, which have more gameplay features but deviate more strongly from the vanilla game. See my profile page for a full list.

Compatibility

See here for a list of (in)compatible mods.

Installation

Installation procedure: Add the mod to your load order and activate it. Make sure you are not currently a vampire. An error message will be shown if another mod is overwriting key Sacrilege scripts.

Uninstallation procedure: Remove the mod. Any perk points in vampire lord perks that have no vanilla equivalent will be lost.

FAQ

• What is the difference between this and Sacrosanct: Sacrilege has fewer features than Sacrosanct, but is more compact and as a result, more balanced. Moreover, Sacrilege focusses more on the drawbacks of Vampiric existence, while Sacrosanct allows you to grow out of them more easily.[/*]

• Does this mod add vampire hunters: No, this is out of scope for a V++ vampire mod. The mod already features enough drawbacks for vampirism.[/*]

D6_SOadO-N0

The beastblood

Hircine's gift inflicted upon mankind is known as the beastblood. It is not only a strength, but also a curse. You gain the following abilities in both mortal and beast form:

• Beastblood: The beastblood grants immunity to disease.[/*]

• Beastblood: The beastblood increases armor by 75 points.[/*]

• Beastblood: The beastblood causes 25% weakness to fire and silver weapons inflict 20 extra damage to you.[/*]

• Call of the Blood: At night, 0-50% (based on the phases of the moon) chance that your curse manifests, forcing you to take the form of the beast.[/*]

• (Argonian) Rabies: Your Argonian blood adds poison damage based on level to your attacks in beast form.[/*]

• (Breton) Skinwalker: Your Breton blood reduces the cooldown of Beast Form by 50%[/*]

• (Dark Elf) Raging Hatred: Your Dark Elven blood extends the duration of Beast Form by 60 seconds.[/*]

• (High Elf) Golden Mane: Your High Elven blood grants 20% resistance to the elements in beast form.[/*]

• (Imperial) Pack Leader: Your Imperial blood reduces the cooldown of howls in beast form by 50%.[/*]

• (Khajiit) Hunting Instinct: Your Khajiit blood reduces the Stamina cost of power attacks in beast form by 20%.[/*]

• (Nord) Vargr: Your Nord blood grants a stacking 25% attack damage for 30 seconds after feeding in beast form.[/*]

• (Orc) Primal Rage: Your Orc blood halves attack damage taken for 15 seconds upon activating Beast Form.[/*]

• (Redguard) Carrion: Your Redguard blood restores 100 points of Health and Stamina when you feed in beast form.[/*]

• (Wood Elf) Moonchaser: Your Wood Elven blood grants 10% extra movement speed in beast form.[/*]

Call of the Blood warns you 15 seconds before you change, giving you time to get clear of populated areas. While forced transformations at night are a feature in older TES games, having them occur at random with no warning only serves to discourage the player from entering cities at night. Equipping Hircine's Ring has the effect of allowing you to "control your transformations", and therefore disables Call of the Blood.

You are more likely to transform at night if the moons are full, and less likely if they are dark.

Rabies will add 15-75 poison damage over 10 seconds to your attack.

You also gain the following power in mortal form:

• Beast Form: Take on the form of the beast for 150 seconds. 90 second cooldown.[/*]

The change from a 1/day power in vanilla Skyrim to a cooldown based power in Growl makes it much more useful. Note that selecting the power during the cooldown still results in a message that it can only be used once a day. This is a Skyrim feature.

Equipping Hircine's Ring reduces the cooldown of Beast Form to 15 seconds.

Werebeasts

Vanilla Skyrim werewolves are underpowered in the late game. They lack survivability, a heal on demand, any useful synergy with mage characters, and even basic features like being able to loot corpses or revert to mortal form at will, forcing players to leave loot behind. Growl includes many buffs and quality of life improvements to make werebeasts viable throughout the game.

Basic stats

You gain the following effects in beast form:

• Carry weight increased by 500 points[/*]

• Take no damage from falls[/*]

• Immune to disease[/*]

• No longer allows players to infinitely knock down enemies with regular power attacks[/*]

• Werebeast attacks deal 10 (+1 per character level) base damage (up to level 50)[/*]

• Werebeast skin grants 50 (+5 per character level) base armor (up to level 50)[/*]

• Werebeast skin grants 10% (+1% per character level) magic resistance (up to level 50)[/*]

• Health increased by 50 points[/*]

• 100% of base Magicka transferred to Stamina instead[/*]

• Move 15% faster[/*]

• Regenerate 20% of maximum Stamina per second[/*]

• Able to feed on humanoid and animal corpses to restore 50 points of Health and extend the remaining duration by 30 seconds[/*]

• Bloodthirst: Werebeast claws do 10 points of bleed damage, healing you for the same amount.[/*]

Raising base Magicka or Stamina both result in more Stamina in beast form. This enables both warriors and mages to effectively make use of beast form. For warriors who do not invest into Magicka at all, transferring their 100 starting Magicka to Stamina results in the same Stamina bonus as in vanilla Skyrim.

Quality of life features

Change back: You can now hold down the power button to change back out of beast form after the 10 second shout cooldown has passed. (Or 30 seconds after a forced transformation at night from the Call of the Blood ability.)

Looting: Werebeasts can now interact with containers, collect ingredients and loot corpses (corpses you can't feed on, such as undead without the Savage Feeding perk, can't be looted). However, lacking opposable thumbs, they cannot pick locks. Take the Totem of the Hunt perk to destroy locks instead.

Shout cooldown: Activating beast form now suspends your active shout cooldown, allowing you to use howls without the shout cooldown getting in your way. When you revert form, the shout cooldown resumes.

Werebeast attacks: Werebeast special attacks no longer have cooldowns associated with them. This is a little known feature in vanilla Skyrim and caused them to not work for seemingly no reason. They have also been updated to feel more impactful; for instance, the knockdown back hand attack now launches targets in an arc instead of straight along the ground.

Growl uses a different and more complex implementation of werebeast looting than most other mods, preventing the loophole found in said other mods where you can equip items and use potions in wereform by opening the loot screen and navigating to your inventory tab at the bottom. This is an exploit and does not belong in a polished vanilla-plus experience.

Scaling and experience gain

A major drawback of werebeasts in vanilla Skyrim is their lack of skill scaling and inability to gain experience. In Growl, werebeasts scale with your highest weapon skill and armor skill:

• In beast form, gain +0.5 damage per level in your highest weapon skill, and +3.0 armor per level in your highest armor skill (up to level 100).[/*]

• In beast form, feed on a corpse to gain experience in your highest weapon skill and armor skill. Experience is based on the corpse's level.[/*]

In the event of a tie between skills, it prioritises One-Handed over Two-Handed over Archery, and Light Armor over Heavy Armor.

At level 50, with level 100 in at least one weapon skill and the Bestial Strength and Improved Bloodthirst perks:

Total attainable damage is (60 base + 50 from skill)*25% = 137.5 (and an additional 30 points of bleed damage)

Total attainable armor is (300 base + 300 from skill) = 600

Total attainable magic resistance is 75

Howls

Werebeasts can howl to create a variety of effects. As in vanilla Skyrim, you start with Howl of Terror. To change to another howl, recover its Totem during the Totems of Hircine quest and activate the Totem. Howls now have a 15 second cooldown.

To use a howl, tap the power button in beast form.

• Howl of Brotherhood: Howl to summon two wolves to your side. If you are a werebear, summons bears instead.[/*]

• Howl of Terror: Howl to cause nearby living targets within 100 feet to flee in terror for 15 seconds.[/*]

• Howl of the Hunt: Howl to detect living targets in a 300 foot radius. This distinguishes between targets that are in combat, searching for you and unaware of you.[/*]

Vanilla Skyrim howls are weak except for the summoning howl. Growl improves the other two by adding their vanilla Skyrim perk effects (increased level cap, ability to distinguish between targets that are in combat or not) to them as a baseline and adding new perks in their place which further improve them. Howl of Terror's duration has additionally been reduced because long duration fear effects tend to be detrimental, forcing you to chase down enemies.

The Werewolf perk tree

Growl expands the Werewolf perk tree from 8 to 19 perks, and the number of Werewolf perk points you can spend from 11 to 27.

To get Werewolf perk points, feed on corpses in beast form. To compensate for the increased number of Werewolf perks, each subsequent level requires only 1 more feeding than the last, down from 2 in vanilla Skyrim.

In version 3.5.0 and 3.6.0, gaining more perks required feeding on stronger corpses. The fifth perk point requires a corpse of at least level 2 and the level requirement increases by 1 every two perk points, up to level 13 for the last perk point. You may have to leave those mangy commoner corpses behind and seek out bandits and other combatants. This feature has been removed in 3.6.1.

• Bestial Strength (4): Deal 10/15/20/25% more attack damage and critical damage in beast form.[/*]

• Animal Vigor: Additional 50 point bonus to Health and Stamina in beast form.[/*]

• Rampage: Beast form lasts 50% longer and feeding extends the duration 50% more.[/*]

• Infinite Duress: Frenzy attacks (one-handed standing power attacks) in beast form stun targets for the duration.[/*]

• Supernatural Strength: Back hand attacks (two-handed standing power attacks) in beast form disarm targets.[/*]

• Roadkill: Leap attacks (two-handed sprinting power attacks) in beast form do a critical strike equal to half your current Stamina and throw targets.[/*]

• Feral Instincts: Power attacks in beast form cost 25% less Stamina and do 25% more damage.[/*]

• Improved Bloodthirst (2): Beast form attacks do an additional 10/20 points of bleed damage, healing you for the same amount.[/*]

• Swipe: Power attacks in beast form can hit multiple targets in front of you.[/*]

• Lycanthropic Speed: Movement speed is increased by 15%, both in and out of beast form.[/*]

• Lycanthropic Regeneration (2): Regenerate an additional 2/4% of your maximum Health and Stamina per second, both in and out of beast form.[/*]

• Spread the Beastblood: Give your follower the beastblood by trading Werebeast Blood with them. No effect on vampires.[/*]

• Totem of Ice Brothers (2): Werebeast Howl of Brotherhood calls Ice Wolves or Snow Bears/Werewolves or Werebears instead.[/*]

• Totem of the Hunt (2): Werebeast Howl of the Hunt shatters locks up to Adept/Expert level at close range.[/*]

• Totem of Terror (2): Werebeast Howl of Terror affects even dragons, forcing them to land for 30/60 seconds.[/*]

• Gorging: Feeding heals 100 points more.[/*]

• Savage Feeding: Able to feed off the undead in beast form, and loot their corpses.[/*]

• Bury the Beast: No longer forced to transform at night.[/*]

• Wolf Among Men: The frequency of Silver Hand Elite werebeast hunters is reduced by 80%.[/*]

The reduced number of feedings per perk point is not retroactive if the mod is installed during a playthrough, but will be applied correctly each time you get a perk point after that. If you have Werewolf perks in vanilla Skyrim, you get the corresponding Growl perks.

Receiving the beastblood

Several ways to get started on your journey:

• Progress through the Companions questline: This is the only way to obtain the beastblood in vanilla Skyrim.[/*]

• Consume the Werebeast Blood: Werebeast Blood is a rare alchemy ingredient that can most often be bought at alchemy vendors (such as Zaria of Grave Concoctions in Falkreath or Elgrim of Elgrim's Elixirs in Riften) and occasionally found in the pockets of warlocks and forsworn or taken from the corpses of wild werewolves.[/*]

• Experience a dream vision: Sleep outdoors under a clear sky at night, and you will have a dream where you can choose to beseech Hircine to grant you the beastblood. This can only occur once.[/*]

These options should appeal to both roleplayers and players who want to jump in as soon as possible, while minimising the impact on your playthrough if you choose not to become a werewolf. This also makes Growl usable in mod packs whose users may not be as interested in details.

Other features

Werebears

You may choose to become a werebear instead of a werewolf.

If you become a werebeast by receiving Hircine's dream vision or consuming Werebeast Blood, a popup allows you to choose between werewolf or werebear form. If you receive the beastblood through the Companions questline, you automatically become a werewolf in accordance with the lore. If you want to change forms at a later time, recover any Totem during the Totems of Hircine quest and activate the Totem.

Version 2.0.0 includes major improvements to werebears. They can now access the Werewolf perk tree without having to change back to werewolf form, the option is available to become a werebear from the beginning, and shifting out of werebear form no longer unequips your armor. Werewolves and werebears are functionally identical, but of course we all know that bears are just better than wolves.

Werebeast hunters

Changing into beast form with witnesses around or leaving a trail of devoured corpses behind may attract the attention of the Silver Hand. Eventually, Silver Hand Elite werebeast hunters will track you down and attack you. Each time another Silver Hand Elite patrol is sent, it includes more and stronger hunters.

World events

Fights between werebeasts and their enemies can now occur in the wilderness at night, making werebeasts a bit more common in the world of Skyrim.

Spreading the beastblood

The perk Spread the Beastblood allows you to give your follower the beastblood by trading them Werebeast Blood and accepting the dialog box. Certain Skyrim characters already have the beastblood.

When a character with the beastblood is your follower, you can ask them to change into beast form in combat. They will turn into a werewolf or werebear depending on which form you have chosen, except for Skyrim characters who are canonically werewolves and will always turn into werewolf form.

The Growl MCM (Mod Configuration Menu)

If you have SkyUI installed, Growl adds a menu to your MCM where you can tweak certain parameters of the mod. Disable (or increase) lunar transformations, werewolf hunters, change experience gain in werebeast form, switch between werewolf and werebear form, etc.

Ring of Hircine

Equipping the Ring of Hircine no longer grants a duplicate Beast Form power with reduced cooldown, but instead directly reduces the cooldown of Beast Form from 90 seconds to 15 seconds.

Compatibility

See here for a list of (in)compatible mods.

Installation

Install: Add the mod to your load order and activate it. Make sure you are not currently transformed into a werewolf.

Uninstall: Remove the mod. Any perk points in werewolf perks that have no vanilla equivalent will be lost.

FAQ

• These bonuses seem too strong: Growl is designed to make werebeasts a viable way to play against all enemies, not just weaker ones. Werebeasts have no items, no enchantments, no blocking, no armor perks, no ranged attack, no potions and no healing magic, and have to deal significant damage to offset these disadvantages. An optimal vanilla character will still match their damage and significantly exceed their survivability. (Note that Growl 3.3.0 does fix a bug that caused excessive amounts of lifesteal.)[/*]

• I have RaceCompatibility and get an integrity error: RaceCompatibility takes precedence over Growl regardless of load order. See the compatibility notes for a workaround.[/*]

• Feeding does not work: This generally means another mod is overwriting the werewolf race, such as Mortal Enemies, causing a conflict. See the compatibility notes for information on how to proceed. Additionally, be aware that the Feed button is the same as the Activate button and therefore grabs and drags corpses if it is held down for too long.[/*]

• Major FPS loss when facing certain objects: This issue is caused by bad assets in other mods, such as Distinct Interiors, with excessively large and detailed collision meshes. This causes the game to slow down when facing those objects as it tries to calculate whether you are in range to activate them. Growl 2.1.0 introduces a workaround where all of the new "activate" features in Growl (such as the ability to loot corpses in beast form) are moved into a separate hidden perk that only exists in beast form. Note that this will alleviate the extra FPS loss from having more activate features than vanilla, but will not fix the FPS loss resulting from said poorly made assets in the first place. Consider removing the mods that exhibit this issue and replacing them with better quality assets.[/*]

• Followers affected by Spread the Beastblood are stuck in beast form: Fixed in Growl 3.4.0. Note that after 3.4.0, followers will still stay in beast form for a minimum of 20 seconds.[/*]

• The Ring of Hircine does not work: Fixed in Growl 3.1.0.[/*]

• Can't open the perk tree in werebear form: Fixed in Growl 2.0.0.[/*]

• I don't get the Beast Form power after feeding: You have a conflicting or broken mod installed.[/*]

• Reverting from Beast Form does not work: You either have a conflicting or broken mod installed, are not holding down the button long enough, or your howls are on cooldown.[/*]

• Beast Form power has a 24 hour cooldown: Fixed in Growl 2.3.0. When updating from earlier versions, you may have to unequip and reequip the power.[/*]

• Looting corpses in beast form unequips all of their gear: Technical limitation. The default loot system in Skyrim would allow players to use potions and equip items from their inventory while looting in beast form, which is easily exploitable and could break beast form, so Growl uses an alternate loot system that disables this loophole but does have some restrictions such as only being able to loot unequipped items.[/*]

• Can't loot quest items in beast form: Technical limitation. Revert out of beast form to loot quest items.[/*]

• Can't loot gold in beast form: When you loot a corpse or container in beast form, the gold is automatically added to your inventory.[/*]

• Can't loot equipped items in beast form: Fixed in Growl 1.0.4.[/*]

• Get Werewolf perk points when looting corpses in mortal form: This appears to be a rare vanilla Skyrim bug.[/*]

• Are the other howls available without going through the questline and recovering the Totems: No, because they are a faction bonus for joining the werewolf faction, much like Vampire Lord form is a faction bonus for joining Harkon.[/*]

sNjWhrP5Q9U iM2JCFj1DrA

DescriptionEver worried about accidentally advancing the wrong skill that contributed to your level? You don’t have to anymore. With this mod, you gain levels by completing quests and exploring the world. Skills no longer provide experience, but they are capped relative to the player’s level for balance purposes (see the skill caps section below). This means you can freely train Lockpicking without gimping your character.

Heavily inspired by Pillars of Eternity leveling and pre 4.0.1 World of Warcraft weapon skill progression system.

Features• Full integration with original experience system and experience bar

• You gain Skyrim's native experience points (there is no secondary XP system)

• No esp file, no scripts, no impact on performance

• Compatible with custom quests and locations

• Compatible with HUD replacers

• Highly customizable (for advanced users)

• Optional "XP from kills" feature

LevelingThe mod uses the vanilla leveling formula (XP required per level is unchanged).

The leveling curve can be adjusted by modifying the original game settings fXPLevelUpBase and fXPLevelUpMult. Other mods that edit these settings are fully compatible and even recommended if you want to experiment with different curves.

XP SourcesThe reward values below are the default configuration. A full list of all available settings and supported location types can be found under the Articles tab on the mod page.

Questing:

Main Quests - 75 XP

College Quests - 50 XP

Thieves Quests - 50 XP

Brotherhood Quests - 50 XP

Companions Quests - 50 XP

Daedric Quests - 75 XP

Side Quests - 50 XP

CivilWar Quests - 75 XP

Dawnguard Quests - 50 XP

Dragonborn Quests - 75 XP

Quest Objectives - 10 XP

Exploring:

Fort - 15 XP

Nordic Ruin - 15 XP

Dwemer Ruin - 20 XP

Shipwreck - 20 XP

Dragon Lair - 30 XP

Doomstone - 20 XP

Imperial Tower - 15 XP

Orc Stronghold - 15 XP

Giant Camp - 20 XP

Nordic Tower - 20 XP

Nordic Dwelling - 20 XP

Daedric Shrine - 30 XP

Default - 10 XP

Clearing:

Cave - 40 XP

Fort - 60 XP

Nordic Ruin - 100 XP

Dwemer Ruin - 100 XP

Dragon Lair - 100 XP

Imperial Tower - 50 XP

Giant Camp - 60 XP

Nordic Tower - 50 XP

Default - 30 XP

Killing:

The final XP reward is calculated from racial XP values and multipliers:

XP = RacialXP * LevelMult * GroupMult

Level multiplier applies a bonus or penalty based on the difference between player and target level:

LevelMult = (EnemyLevel / PlayerLevel) ^ LevelFactor

Group multiplier reduces the reward depending on the number of followers:

https://i.imgur.com/Heh9jsl.png

Racial XP values can be changed in the INI file located in: \SKSE\Plugins\Experience\Races

Custom races are not supported by default and require compatibility patches. Multiple patches can be loaded at once without limitation.

Reading:

XP is awarded based on the value of the book when reading non-skill and non-spell books:

https://i.imgur.com/8OdABsa.png

Skill CapsSkills train as in vanilla Skyrim but are capped relative to the player’s level for balance.

https://i.imgur.com/P5pewoW.pngBy default, all skills cap at 18, with the cap increasing by 2 for each player level.

Example:

Level 1 = 20 (18 + 2)

Level 5 = 28 (18 + 10)

Racial skill bonuses are added on top of the base cap for each skill. For example, Nords have +10 in Two-Handed; at level 1 their Two-Handed cap will be 30 instead of 20. Racial caps are optional and can be disabled in the config.

Base cap progression (intermediate values are scaled dynamically):+--------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+

| Player | 01-05 | 06-10 | 11-15 | 16-20 | 21-25 | 26-30 | 31-35 | 36-40 |

+--------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+

| Skills |  >20  |  >30  |  >40  |  >50  |  >60  |  >70  |  >80  |  >90  |

+--------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+

CompatibilityMinor incompatibility with mods that replace statsmenu.swf and trainingmenu.swf - mod authors check this article for more info

Compatible with custom quests and custom discoverable/clearable locations

Compatible with gameplay and perk overhauls

RecommendedExperience - MCM - adds Mod Configuration Menu (MCM) support, requires SkyUI

Experience Synthesis Patcher - makes your whole load order compatible with 'killing' feature, requires manual tweaking

Experience Quests Tweak - reclassifies vanilla 'None' quests to correct type to make them more compatible with this mod

No Startup Quest XP - sets type of some modded utility quests to 'None' to prevent startup XP spam

Leveling Freedom - fully customize the leveling curve via MCM menu

Downgrade Patcher - if you accidentally updated to Skyrim Fishing Edition

FAQQ: I’m still getting XP from skills, is the mod broken?

A: It requires SKSE64. Make sure you have the correct version installed.

Q: Do I need to start a new game?

A: No. It works mid-game, but you will not gain XP for quests already completed.

Q: Do I need to clean save when updating?

A: No. It’s an SKSE plugin, so it can be enabled, disabled, or updated at any time without breaking saves.

Q: I can't level up. I get the notification but level up option is not here!

A: That’s a core feature of Survival Mode: you can only level up after sleeping. It’s not caused by this mod.

Q: My skill bars are all orange, what should I do?

A: Ensure your statsmenu.swf is compatible with current version (some UI replacers and patches may be outdated).

Q: I changed related settings mid-play and now my skill cap values are wrong.

A: You need to level up or use setlevel <your_level_plus_one> followed by setlevel <your_original_level> to recalculate the skill cap.CreditsNightfallstorm - VR update, trainingmenu implementation, fixing legendary icons and VR version testing

Q: Is this mod compatible with <insert mod>?

A: Most likely, yes. I have tried to make it so conflicts will be at an absolute minimum. I also left all quest scripts alone, which should make sure this won't conflict with those. Only thing I can think of, that could potentially conflict, is if a mod changes the stage at which a quest completes, but from my experience, I haven't found such mods.

Q: Does installing/updating/uninstalling on an existing save work? / I already completed some of these quests in my playthrough. Is it safe to install?

A: See console commands above.

Q: Could you add more unique effects, instead of perk points?

This could be exploited and as such, I would prefer not to mess with it. As for the Civil War: That questline is quite buggy, so I'd rather not touch it, in case I break anything.

Q: Will you make a patch for <insert mod>?

A: Only if it's a mod I use myself or plan on using, I have enough time and I actually like the idea. Otherwise, feel free to do it yourself. (see permissions)

Q: I have a suggestion to improve the mod. Can you do it?

A: Maybe, if I have time and I like the idea, I'll consider it.

Q: Will you port this to <insert platform>?

A: No, I myself only support the Steam and GOG English SE and AE versions of Skyrim. If someone else wants to port it, feel free. (see permission) If you decide to port it, you yourself take full responsibility to offer support to said port. I will not provide no support for any ports by third parties.

Q: I use a ported version of this mod on <insert platform> and I have a problem. Can you help?

A: I don't provide any support for third party ports on other platforms than the Steam and GOG English SE and AE versions of Skyrim. If you have issues, you should adress the person that ported it.

Q: Does this work on Skyrim 1.6+, aka "Anniversary Edition"?

A: Yes, it should.

Q: Why don't your mods use MCMs and instead use this janky console command system to set globals?

A: I am not a fan of MCMs. You can set the globals by making a patch in xEdit. I have no plans of changing this. If you want to add an MCM, feel free. (see permissions)

Q: Why don't you use FOMODs?

A: That would require reuploading the entire mod, in question, even if I only make a small change. My internet is limited and reuploading

the files each time will take a huge chunk of my monthly volume. Given the amount of modules within this mod and the relative small

filesize of all of the modules combined, I've made an exception for this mod.

Apothecary - An Alchemy Overhaul

Apothecary is a complete overhaul of Skyrim’s alchemy system designed to balance existing potions and poisons while adding powerful new effects to the game. The mod normalizes the magnitude of all alchemical ingredients in order to eliminate the gameplay loop of checking UESP to see which effects have slightly higher potencies, or chasing Salmon Roe to level up. It also significantly reduces the gold value of both player-created potions and generic potions while ensuring that the player still levels at a faster rate than Vanilla. In addition, the mod rebalances generic potions so that their strongest and weakest variants match the potency of player-created potions. Finally, Apothecary removes several useless or poorly implemented effects in order to make room for more interesting new effects without adding new ingredients.

Apothecary does not require my other mods, but it is designed to be consistent with them. For instance, Apothecary adds poisons for each of the new Illusion archetypes and several of the new Alteration archetypes added by Mysticism - A Magic Overhaul.

Notes

• Damage Health, Magicka, and Stamina poisons deal (stacking) damage over time.

• Lingering damage poisons are still clearly differentiated from other poisons.

• Poisons replicate all of Illusion’s influence effects, including new archetypes added by Mysticism, allowing poison-focused characters to manipulate the battlefield.

• Poisons replicate all the new debuff effects added to Alteration by Mysticism, with higher potencies to compensate for their one-time-use nature.

• All Poisons benefit from Weakness to Poison, allowing you to increase the strength of poisons such as Damage Armor, Fear, and Weakness to Magic.

Scrambled Bugs - Poison Resistance Patch

In Skyrim, all poisons are automatically resisted by Poison Resistance, no matter what value is placed in the "Resisted By" field in their Magic Effects. This means that poisons such as Burden and Weakness to Fire are weaker against targets with high Poison Resistance, and stronger against targets with low Poison Resistance. It also means that Poisons of Weakness to Poison can be stacked infinitely, leading to ridiculous effects. Because of this, in earlier versions of Apothecary, debuff poisons were quite weak, because we had to assume the player was using Weakness to Poison effects to buff their strength considerably.

However, Scrambled Bugs now comes with a "Poison Resistance" patch that allows us to create poisons that aren't resisted by Poison Resistance. This allows us to balance debuff poisons such as Damage Armor and Weakness to Frost in much the same way that we balance similar spells in Mysticism. It also allows the Weakness to Poison effect to exist without stacking with itself infinitely.

We strongly recommend that you download Scrambled Bugs and turn the "Poison Resistance" patch on. With the patch activated, poisons of Burden, Damage Weapon, Damage Armor, Weakness to Fire, Weakness to Frost, and Weakness to Shock will be fully resisted by an enemy with 100% Poison Resistance, since they are considered "immune" to Poisons. However, once you reduce an enemy's Poison Resistance to any value below 100%, debuff poisons will produce their full effect (this is similar to how Mysticism balances debuff spells). In addition, poisons of Weakness to Poison will work on targets even with 100% Poison Resistance, allowing alchemists to affect highly resistant enemies without resorting to other skills such as Enchanting or Alteration. This also solves the problem where poisons of Weakness to Poison are ineffective on the very enemies you'd most like to use them on.

With the Poison Resistance patch activated, Poisons of Damage Health, Damage Magicka, Damage Stamina, Lingering Damage Health, Lingering Damage Magicka, Lingering Damage Stamina, Calm, Frenzy, Silence, Fear, Paralysis, and Command continue to scale on Poison Resistance, meaning these poisons will be less effective against an enemy with high Poison Resistance and more effective against an enemy with low Poison Resistance.

General Changes and Removed Effects

Apothecary removes several potion effects from the game. Sometimes, these potion effects were removed for balance reasons (Fortify Smithing and Fortify Enchanting); sometimes, they were only removed because they were redundant with a new or existing effect (Damage Magicka Regeneration, Fortify Light Armor). Removing these effects allowed us to add our new effects with minimizing changes to existing recipes, so most of the combinations you remember will still work fine. However, in a few places, we did make changes to existing effects, and we do welcome feedback as to whether some effects feel rarer than they should be. We also changed the rarity of a few ingredients. Now that we’ve normalized the magnitude of all potion archetypes, it simply doesn’t make sense for items like Salmon Roe to be as rare as they are. Finally, we tweaked Sinderion's Serendipity (it's called Sinderion's Legacy now) to be a little more desirable and to work better with perk overhauls.

A list of removed effects can be found below.

Fortify Enchanting

Compatibility

Apothecary is not compatible with other alchemy overhauls. You will need a patch for any mod that adds new ingredients, in order to adjust their magnitudes, durations, and gold values to be in line with Apothecary. Apothecary may also have some minor compatibility issues with mods that add new player-crafted enchantments. This is because both alchemy and enchanting mods need to make use of the same “Unused Actor Values” to implement their effects. The incompatibility should be limited to specific enchantments that use the same actor values as Apothecary.

items.name: Thaumaturgy - An Enchanting Overhaul
items.description:
Thaumaturgy - An Enchanting Overhaul

Thaumaturgy is a complete overhaul of Skyrim’s enchanting system designed to balance existing enchantments and add powerful new weapon and armor enchantments to the game. By leveraging Skyrim’s slot restriction mechanic, Thaumaturgy is able to fix several of the problems with Vanilla enchanting (such as 100% cost reduction) while still ensuring that each individual enchantment feels meaningful. Thaumaturgy also removes some useless or bugged enchantments, eliminates the crafting loop, adds missing generic items to the loot lists, and ensures that generic items are equal in strength to player-created enchantments.

Thaumaturgy does not require my other mods, but it is designed to be consistent with them. For instance, Thaumaturgy adds weapon enchantments for several of Mysticism’s Alteration and Illusion archetypes, and some of the new armor enchantments mirror the potion effects added by Apothecary.

Weapon Enchantments

The magnitudes in the following list reflect the strength of an enchantment created by a character with 100 Enchanting and all of the Vanilla perks. Generic enchantments have been reworked to be consistent with player-created enchantments at all levels.

Fire Damage - Deals 30 Fire damage. Targets on fire take extra damage over time.

Frost Damage - Deals 30 Frost damage to Health and Stamina.

Shock Damage - Deals 30 Shock damage to Health and Magicka.

Chaos Damage - Has a 50% chance to deal 30 Fire, Frost, or Shock Damage.

Magicka Damage - Deals 10 Magicka damage per second for 10 seconds.

Stamina Damage - Deals 10 Stamina damage per second for 10 seconds.

Absorb Health - Absorbs 30 Health from living targets.

Absorb Magicka - Absorbs 30 Magicka.

Absorb Stamina - Absorbs 30 Stamina.

Sun Damage - Deals 40 Sun damage to the undead. Targets on fire take extra damage over time.

Poison Damage - Deals 5 Poison damage per second for 10 seconds.

Turn Undead - Undead up to level 40 have a 25% chance to be turned for 30 seconds.

Burden - Reduces enemy Movement and Attack Speed by 25% for 30 seconds.

Damage Weapon - Reduces enemy weapon damage by 25% for 30 seconds.

Damage Armor - Reduces enemy Armor Rating by 150 for 30 seconds.

Weakness to Fire - Reduces enemy Fire Resistance by 50% for 30 seconds.

Weakness to Frost - Reduces enemy Frost Resistance by 50% for 30 seconds.

Weakness to Shock - Reduces enemy Shock Resistance by 50% for 30 seconds.

Weakness to Poison - Reduces enemy Poison Resistance by 50% for 30 seconds.

Silence - Living targets up to level 40 have a 25% chance to be silenced for 30 seconds.

Paralyze - Living targets up to level 40 have a 25% chance to be paralyzed for 10 seconds.

Fear - Living targets up to level 40 have a 25% chance to flee from combat for 30 seconds.

Frenzy - Living targets up to level 40 have a 25% chance to attack anyone nearby for 30 seconds.

Banish - Daedra up to level 40 have a 25% chance to be banished.

Soul Trap - Fills a soul gem if the target dies within 30 seconds.

Damage Construct - Deals 10 Magic damage per second for 10 seconds to Dwarven automatons.

Huntsman's Prowess - Deals 40 Magic damage to animals.

Silent Moons - At night, absorbs 30 Health.

Notes

• Damage values for Fire, Frost, and Shock damage are (mostly) equal to Vanilla. The incredible power creep that was possible in Vanilla did not come from enchanting itself, but from outside effects such as the crafting loop and Destruction perks.

• Absorb Magicka and Stamina will no longer work on characters who have no Magicka or Stamina to absorb.

• Weakness to Fire, Frost, Shock, and Poison allow spellswords to buff the damage of their spells. Weakness to Poison is especially suited to alchemists, since it allows poisons to affect enemies such as Draugr and automatons.

• Turn Undead, Banish, and Illusion enchantments now all have a 25% chance to trigger. Power Attacking increases this chance to 50%, and also doubles the target level of the enchantment.

• Scrambled Bugs is recommended in order to ensure that Chaos Damage scales properly with Enchanting skill.

Armor Enchantments

The magnitudes in the following list reflect the strength of an enchantment created by a character with 100 Enchanting and all of the Vanilla perks. Generic enchantments have been reworked to be consistent with player-created enchantments at all levels. The armor slots on which these enchantments can be placed are listed in parenthesis. No distinction is made between armor and robes, or between circlets, hoods, and helmets.

Fortify Alteration Cost (Head, Chest) - Your Alteration spells cost 25% less.

Fortify Conjuration Cost (Head, Chest) - Your Conjuration spells cost 25% less.

Fortify Destruction Cost (Head, Chest) - Your Destruction spells cost 25% less.

Fortify Illusion Cost  (Head, Chest) - Your Illusion spells cost 25% less.

Fortify Restoration Cost  (Head, Chest) - Your Restoration spells cost 25% less.

Fortify Destruction Power (Necklace, Ring) - Your Destruction spells are 25% stronger.

Fortify Illusion Power (Necklace, Ring) - Your Illusion spells are 25% stronger.

Fortify Restoration Power (Necklace, Ring) - Your Restoration spells are 25% stronger.

Fortify Alteration Duration (Necklace, Ring) - Your Alteration spells last 50% longer.

Fortify Conjuration Duration (Necklace, Ring) - Your Conjuration spells last 50% longer.

Fortify Illusion Duration (Necklace, Ring) - Your Illusion spells last 50% longer.

Fortify Restoration Duration (Necklace, Ring) - Your Restoration spells last 50% longer.

Fortify One-handed (Gloves, Ring) - You deal 25% extra damage with One-handed weapons.

Fortify Two-handed (Gloves, Ring) - You deal 25% extra damage with Two-handed weapons.

Fortify Archery (Head, Necklace) - You deal 25% extra damage with ranged weapons.

Fortify Unarmed (Gloves, Ring) - You deal 25% extra unarmed damage.

Fortify Shout Power (Head, Ring) - Your Shouts are 25% stronger.

Fortify Shout Duration (Necklace, Chest) - Your Shouts last 50% longer.

Fortify Block (Head, Necklace, Shield) - You block 25% more damage.

Fortify Armor Rating (Head, Chest, Shield) - Your Armor Rating is increased by 100.

Reflect Damage (Head, Chest, Shield) - You reflect 50% of incoming melee damage back at your attacker.

Fortify Power Attacks (Head, Chest) - You deal 25% more damage with power attacks.

Fortify Sneak Attacks (Gloves, Ring) - You deal 25% more damage with sneak attacks and spells.

Fortify Potion Duration (Head, Gloves) - Your potions last 50% longer.

Fortify Poison Use (Head, Ring) - Your poisons last for 50% more hits.

Fortify Bash Damage (Shield) - You deal 100% more damage with bashes.

Resist Arrow Damage (Shield) - You resist 50% of incoming arrow damage while blocking.

Resist Power Attack Damage (Shield) - You resist 50% of incoming power attack damage while blocking.

Resist Spell Damage (Shield) - You resist 50% of incoming spell damage while blocking.

Fortify Barter (Head, Necklace) - You receive 20% better prices.

Fortify Security (Gloves, Ring) - You are 25% better at lockpicking and pickpocketing.

Fortify Sneak (Ring, Boots) - You are 25% better at sneaking.

Fortify Carry Weight (Necklace, Boots) - Your Carry Weight is increased by 50.

Fortify Health (Head, Necklace, Chest, Ring, Shield) - Your Health is increased by 50.

Fortify Magicka (Head, Necklace, Gloves, Ring) - Your Magicka is increased by 50.

Fortify Stamina (Necklace, Chest, Ring, Boots) - Your Stamina is increased by 50.

Fortify Health Regeneration (Head, Necklace, Chest, Ring, Shield) - Your Health Regeneration is increased by 50%.

Fortify Magicka Regeneration (Necklace, Chest, Gloves, Ring) - Your Magicka Regeneration is increased by 50%.

Fortify Stamina Regeneration (Head, Necklace, Ring, Boots) - Your Stamina Regeneration is increased by 50%.

Resist Fire (Necklace, Gloves, Ring, Boots, Shield) - Your Fire Resistance is increased by 50%.

Resist Frost (Necklace, Gloves, Ring, Boots, Shield) - Your Frost Resistance is increased by 50%.

Resist Shock (Necklace, Gloves, Ring, Boots, Shield) - Your Shock Resistance is increased by 50%.

Resist Poison (Necklace, Gloves, Chest, Ring, Shield) - Your Poison Resistance is increased by 50%.

Resist Magic (Necklace, Chest, Ring, Shield) - Your Magic Resistance is increased by 25%.

Resist Disease (Necklace, Ring) - Your Disease Resistance is increased by 100%.

Waterbreathing (Head, Necklace) - You can breathe underwater.

Light (Head, Necklace) - You create a light that illuminates nearby objects.

Slowfall (Boot) - You take 50% less damage from falling.

Muffle (Boots) - You make 50% less noise while moving.

Waterwalking (Boots) - You can walk on water.

Notes

• Most skill enchantments can only be placed on two items, reducing the massive power creep offered by armor enchantments. This change also encourages players to pursue more diverse enchantments rather than stacking the same two enchantments over and over again.

• Magnitude values for Fortify One-handed, Fortify Two-handed, and Fortify Marksman were extremely high in Vanilla and have been significantly reduced.

• Armor enchantments stack additively with their alchemical counterparts, reducing the power creep that occurred when combining both alchemy and enchanting on a single character.

• Enchantments that fortify Health, Magicka, Stamina, Health Regeneration, Magicka Regeneration, and Stamina Regeneration are slightly weaker than in Vanilla. However, unlike in Vanilla, pre-enchanted items will not be two or three times more powerful than player enchanted items.

• Scrambled Bugs is recommended in order to allow Reflect Damage to stack beyond 100%.

Mage Gear

When standardizing the value of player-created and generic enchantments, one of the difficulties that we encountered was that mage gear, especially gear with Magicka Regeneration as an enchantment, was extremely common in Skyrim. Furthermore, the values on these enchantments were extremely high. Items with 50% Magicka Regeneration can be found just laying around, free for the taking, despite the fact that a Master Enchanter could only put 62% Magicka Regeneration on an item in Vanilla. Over time, I’ve started to suspect that someone at Bethesda knew that Skyrim’s magic balance was pretty poor, and one strategy that they employed to fix this problem was throwing overpowered mage gear at the players. (Think about the fact that you get a Novice Hood and Novice Robes in Helgen and then you are immediately given another Novice Hood and an even better robe as soon as you get to the College.)

After extensive playtesting, I believe that Simonrim (and other mod suites) addresses the core problems of magic balance, and that overcompensating from gear is no longer a desirable strategy. Because of that, I’ve made some changes to low level mage gear.

• Basic mage robes (especially the blue and black robes you see everywhere) are no longer enchanted.

• Other types of clothing and robes that used to have a 50% Magicka Regeneration enchantment now have a 25% Magicka Regeneration enchantment.

• College robes with school-based enchantments have reduced Magicka Regeneration. To compensate for this nerf, they have a unique enchantment that gives 25% cost reduction to level-appropriate spells from their specific school. For instance, Apprentice Robes of Illusion reduce the cost of all Novice and Apprentice Illusion spells by 25%.

• College robes without a school based enchantment are no longer enchanted. These robes were always worse than robes with school-based enchantments, so I don’t believe this is a very big loss. Also, you can use these robes to make your own enchanted versions of the College robes. This is a quality of life tweak I’ve always wanted as a player, so I hope you like it too.

Thaumaturgy - Jump Boots Addon

This plugin changes the Slowfall Enchantment into a Fortify Acrobatics Enchantment, which doubles your jump height and reduces your fall damage by 50%. This is a non-scaling enchantment that can only be placed on boots. Additionally, this plugin also turns the Predator's Grace boots into a special artifact. These boots increase your jump height by five times and reduce your fall damage by 50%. Finally, if you have the Mysticism - Jump Spell Addon, casting the spell Leap or Slowfall while wearing boots will cause the effects to stack together multiplicatively.

I added these spells and enchantments because it's fun to jump over houses, but it is possible to use them to get into some trouble. You can probably jump over the walls of a city and, without Open Cities or a similar mod installed, find yourself in a strange alternate version of the town, or you might skip a trigger box or otherwise sequence break a quest mod. There's very little risk of permanent harm, but please enjoy these spells responsibly.

Thaumaturgy - Weapon Enchantment XP Tweak

Disenchanting weapons gives you very little XP, and fixing this problem through an ESP is both very difficult and quite incompatible. Therefore, Thaumaturgy now comes with an optional DLL to increase the XP you gain from disenchanting weapons by 15 times. This causes weapons to give XP that is more similar to the XP granted from disenchanting armors, and it also does wonders for leveling your enchanting higher without annoying, repetitive grinding. This DLL requires Address Library, and comes in a FOMOD with 1.5.97 and 1.6+ versions available. In addition, there's no dependency on Thaumaturgy for this DLL, so you can use it along with Summermyst to solve the same issue.

Compatibility

Thaumaturgy is not compatible with other enchanting overhauls, including Summermyst, and no patches will be provided. Some mods that need to adjust armor stats, templates, or leveled lists may step on Thaumaturgy's toes. Usually these conflicts should be relatively minor. We have provided a patch for WACCF and may provide other patches upon request.

Thaumaturgy should be roughly compatible with any mod that adds armor or weapons. New enchantments will not be generated on new armors and weapons, but existing enchantments should function as expected. Due to the near-infinite number of these types of mods, it is unlikely I will provide patches.

Thaumaturgy should be compatible with any perk overhaul. If you encounter any specific problems, bring them to my attention and I will investigate whether a patch is required.
